text:
alex_m: FYI bringing up calypso18b (int4) on canary cluster, hitting intermittent OOMs when serving longer generation jobs. started with batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=1024. :thinking:
priya_k: ugh. any logs? frag vs real OOM?
alex_m: logs show allocator failure + kv cache surge. snippet below:
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] model=calypso18b-int4 instance=p4a-gn5 worker=3
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] kv_cache_alloc attempted=1.2GB available=800MB
```
danielle: that looks like memory fragmentation — int4 reduces model memory but increases peak allocation churn for long kv sequences. try lowering max_new_tokens default to 256 for canary. also reduce batch_size to 2 or use windowed batching.
samir: quick config to try (canary route):
```
{
  "route": "calypso18b-canary",
  "batching": {"max_batch_size": 2, "max_latency_ms": 60, "window_ms": 6},
  "defaults": {"max_new_tokens": 256, "prefetch_kv": true, "kv_trim_threshold": 0.6}
}
```
alex_m: deploying that now to canary. will enable kv_trim_threshold to evict older prefixes earlier.
infra-bot: Deploy started by alex_m for service calypso18b-canary at revision r-20260318-12. ETA ~2m.
priya_k: also recommend enabling temporary fallback to calypso18b-fp16 for long-running jobs so we avoid customer-facing errors while we tune. routing policy: prefer int4 but fallback to fp16 when predicted token_count > 512.
danielle: good idea. we should also add an eval slice specifically for conversational prompts with long context to catch regressions. cc @samir for eval harness.
samir: I'll spin up an eval job against the canary set with 200 samples length 800-1200 tokens and run quality/latency bench. linking dashboard: https://internal-dash/redwood/calypso18b/canary (metrics will populate) :eyes: 
alex_m: quick note — saw one instance where prefetched kv allocation failed when max_new_tokens was 1024 even with free memory reported ~1.5GB. that matches fragmentation hypothesis.
priya_k: for production defaults we probably want max_new_tokens=256 and a canary rollout window that scales to 512 if KV cache pattern is stable. add a regression alert on perplexity + token latency.
danielle: opened ticket INF-4821 to track tuning, eviction heuristics, and fallback policy. owner: danielle. ETA EOW.
alex_m: deploy finished. monitoring for 10m then run eval. will post results. :thumbsup:
priya_k: cheers — if we still see OOMs after lowering defaults, we should try adjusting allocator flags (cuda malloc async / memory pool) and test a small quant calib tweak (hybrid int4/int8 for attention weights).
infra-bot: Alert: 1 minor OOM observed at 2026-03-18T14:20:12Z on node p4a-gn5-17. auto-retry succeeded.
alex_m: saw that — looks like one leftover spike during warmup. continuing to watch.
samir: eval run completed (quick pass): 200 samples, mean latency +20% vs fp16 on 1k tokens, 98% successful, 2 reroutes to fp16 due to allocation failures. uploading logs to: https://s3.internal/redwood/calypso18b/evals/20260318-run1
priya_k: solid. action items: 1) keep canary defaults at max_new_tokens=256, 2) add fallback rule >512 tokens -> fp16, 3) run allocator tuning next week, 4) add eval slice for long-context. assigning to owners in INF-4821.
danielle: noted. will also add a short doc in eng-ml/wiki about int4 frag signals and kv_trim heuristics so onboards are faster.
alex_m: thanks all — will update thread with perf numbers after 1h of canary traffic.
